steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: A computer network is two or more computers and other devices connected together to share data, information, and resources. | Definition: A PAN is a network that connects devices within a very small range, typically within a few metres of an individual person. | Definition: A LAN is a network that covers a small geographical area, such as a single building, office, school, or home. LANs are typically owned and managed by the organisation that uses them. | Definition: A WAN is a network that covers a large geographical area, such as a city, country, or the whole world. WANs typically connect multiple LANs together over long distances.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Define PAN, LAN, and WAN, giving an example of each. | Compare Ethernet and Wi-Fi, giving two advantages and two disadvantages of each. | Give three advantages and three disadvantages of using a computer network.
